title: Church music, war work and the road into the music business
summary: He grew up on church music, worked in aircraft plants in Los Angeles and Buffalo during the war, then returned to open a nightclub.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: When you were growing up, what music, who'd you listen to when you were growing up?

Well, in that particular time, most things you were listening was church music, you know. I played choir, the lady who played for the choir, you know. Because in them days, rock and roll wasn't happening, the blues wasn't happening, not to the young people had to go to church, you know, and that's all they really was interested in, you know. So I tried music for quite about two or three years and I never could play it. But then I came to New Orleans, and it was years passed, so I got older and older and older, you know. So I went to Los Angeles during the war, World War II, and I was in the hotel business out there, and I made very good money, so I came back and overnight club here in New Orleans. And that's when I got really hooked into the music business.
Well, what did you, what other jobs did you have?
Well, before the music business? Yeah. Well, I was in the Duggars Aircraft during the war time, and after the war, I lived in Buffalo, I worked for Weston House.
I was a motor inspector for them in Buffalo. Oh. And I was a loomer tester for Duggars Aircraft in New Orleans. I mean, say, in Los Angeles.
So I came back there in our open night club in Coase Quai, and that's-
